messages:
alex: @oncall quick Q — if we need to do a surgical kill for the recommender feature in prod, who is authorized to flip the toggle? Also what’s the exact console path / CLI command and the audit id format we should paste in the postmortem? :rotating_light:

maria: For PROD emergency: SRE oncall, the engineering incident lead, and Security on-call are authorized. Prefer the Console path first since it produces a full, immutable audit record: Console > Feature Toggles > recommender > Emergency OFF. Use CLI only if console is unavailable.

kevin: CLI example (returns an audit_id):
```
redwood-ops toggle set --env prod --flag recommender --value off --reason "incident-4567: high latencies"
# outputs: audit_id=aud_20260318_abc123
```

alex: Does the CLI require MFA/2FA? Where does that audit_id get stored?

maria: Yes — CLI uses our SSO + device MFA. The audit_id is returned in stdout and also recorded in the Flags Audit service (/audit/flags) with 365d retention. Paste the audit_id + short rationale into the incident doc immediately after flipping.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: NOTE: Any flagged prod flip will trigger pages to eng-oncall and sec-notify, and will be recorded as a P0 action per policy.

ops-jen: If you only need a regional cutoff use `--scope=region:us-west-2`. Default behavior is global; be explicit. Also `--dry-run` is available for staging.

kevin: A few CLI notes: 1) the CLI prompts for a confirm unless you pass `--force-confirm`. 2) include `--actor-email` if acting on someone else's behalf. 3) keep the exact `audit_id` — it's the canonical proof.

maria: Post-flip checklist (quick):
1) Verify traffic reroute — check `recommender.health` and 200s/5xx in last 5m.
2) Confirm 95p latency is back within SLOs.
3) Validate canary audience metrics (dashboard: /dash/recommender/canary) are stable.
4) Capture `audit_id` + attach to incident doc and slack thread.

alex: Who signs off to re-enable? Is it incident lead + product required?

maria: Re-enable requires: incident lead (engineering) + one senior SRE + product PM ack in-thread. If Security initiated the flip, Security must also ACK. We keep the flag off for at least 30 minutes unless we have proof it’s safe to bring back immediately.

kevin: Audit trail formatting we expect in the postmortem: `audit_id | actor | method (console/cli) | scope | timestamp | short reason` — paste that as a single line.

alex: If I flip now I’ll ping @maria and paste the audit id here. Also annotating the control ticket.

ops-jen: And add a note to the change-control ticket. If customers could be impacted, tag `#regulatory-watch` and notify CSMs.

sre-lead: One more operational point: we should schedule quarterly kill-switch rehearsals for the ops and oncall teams — small scoped drills so people know the paths (console vs CLI) and can capture audit_ids properly.

maria: Agreed — I’ll add a short appendix to the runbook: exact console clicks, sample CLI, expected audit_id format, example postmortem snippet, how to prove flip worked (small curl to `/recommender/health?canary=true`), and re-enable signoff template.

alex: Great, filing the incident doc now and will run the drill notes later. Thanks all :thumbsup:
